newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Monteiro Aranha to sell stake in Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Monteiro Aranha to sell stake in Ericsson.

text.p: Brazilian industrial group Monteiro Aranha said it plans to sell a block of preferred shares in Ericsson Telecomunicacoes, a company official said.

A group source said Monteiro Aranha President Olavo Monteiro de Carvalho and other group officers were due to hold a news conference at 1600 local time/1900 gmt at Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana Palace Hotel to announce the transaction.
The source could not say when the sale would take place or how many shares would be sold.
But local news agency Invest News said the group intended to sell its entire 54 percent stake in Ericsson to raise funds to invest in cellular phones. The report could not be independently confirmed.
Ericsson Telecomunicacoes is the Brazilian unit of Swedish telecoms equipment giant Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson, which aims be a major supplier to Brazil's new private telecom operators.
Monteiro Aranha is a member of the Brascom consortium bidding on concessions to operate cellular services on Brazil's B Band frequency, which is now being privatized.
Other members of the consortium are Brazilian construction firm Andrade Gutierrez, Southwestern Bell of the United States and cellular operator Mannesmann Eurokom of Germany.
The group has bid on six B Band concessions in Brazil, including the coveted areas of Sao Paulo city and state, Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states and Minas Gerais state.
